paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this chapter. Over and over the text says it: "just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:5, 21, 26, 29, 31) The workers don't improve the plan or add their own flair. They trust that what God asked for is worth doing exactly the way He asked.

Now look at who the garments are for. Names of the sons of Israel are engraved on the stones on the shoulder pieces, and on the twelve stones of the breastpiece (Exodus 39:6-7, 14). The priest carries those names, and I think that's a picture of being held. Then comes the gold plate on the turban: HOLY TO THE LORD (Exodus 39:30). The first thing people see on the priest is that he belongs to God.

And when everything is done, Moses inspects ALL of it, and what does he do? He blesses them (Exodus 39:43). Not a lecture, not a list of fixes. A blessing. So bake like that, friend. Do what God says the way He says it, even the small stuff nobody will notice, because He sees every stitch, and He's the One who blesses.
